Subscribe Health News Florida Florida reports fewer dengue investigations but Tampa Bay outbreak persists WUSF | By Rick Mayer Published November 13, 2026 at 5:32 PM EST Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email Felipe Dana / AP Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, the species responsible for transmitting dengue fever, sit in a petri dish in a lab. Transmission typically occurs when a female acquires the virus while biting an infected human, then passes it to another person through a subsequent bite. Hillsborough, Pinellas and Pasco accounted for 92 of Florida’s 100 new locally acquired infections in the most recent report. However, the number of cases the health department has under review decreased in recent weeks. The number of new locally acquired dengue cases under investigation has decreased in recent weeks, the Florida Department of Health said Friday. However, the agency’s weekly update of confirmed cases shows significant activity in the Tampa Bay area, where an outbreak of the mosquito-borne disease continues. Hillsborough, Pinellas and Pasco counties accounted for 92 of the state’s 100 locally acquired dengue illnesses reported the week of Nov. 1-7. “As investigations are completed, updates will be reflected in the weekly case counts,” the health department said. Hillsborough remains the center of the spread, with 61 new cases over the latest period. The county had shown a steady decrease in infections, with only 62 all of October. Last week’s update, covering Oct. 25-31, recorded only 22 new cases, the fewest since August. Hillsborough has totaled 468 infections since the onset in July. That includes the death of an 80-year-old Tampa woman in September. County Administrator Bonnie Wise extended a local state of emergency due to dengue through Nov. 19. Emergencies expire every seven days unless extended. “The areas of concern for disease transmission requiring mitigation efforts currently encompass over one-half of Hillsborough County and are continuing to spread,” Wise’s emergency order said. ALSO READ: How Florida became the epicenter of localized U.S. dengue cases and what role climate played Pinellas’ total has been slowly inching upward. The county added 29 in the latest report, its biggest weekly count this year. Pinellas recorded 54 last month, essentially half of its 109 total counted since the onset in August. There were two new cases in Pasco, for a total of six. The state total since the onset in July is 624. Orange and Miami-Dade each increased by four this past week. Contributing to the problem: cases associated with travel to regions of the world where the disease is endemic. The state database added 40 cases of international-travel dengue during the week of Nov. 1-7, bringing the total to 422 for the year. Health experts advise these numbers are likely undercounts. Symptoms don’t usually begin until about two weeks after someone is bitten by an infected mosquito. Many infected people don’t even get sick. And there is typically a delay from when symptoms begin and when a case is reported by the health department. The virus is spread by Aedes mosquitoes, a species common in Florida. Transmission typically occurs when a female acquires the virus while biting an infected human, then passes it to another person through a subsequent bite. The Florida outbreak is the largest in the United States in decades, health officials have said. Previously, the most Florida cases were 199 in 2023. Last year, the state reported 62 cases. ALSO READ: When a mosquito control expert flunks your home during a dengue inspection People with dengue can feel as though they have the flu, with severe muscle aches, headaches, joint pain, fever and occasional rashes. Hospitalization is common for severe cases, which may include bleeding, shock or even death. Health officials advise residents going outside to apply repellent and wear long pants and sleeves to help prevent mosquito bites. As of Nov. 7, county mosquito-borne illness alerts are in effect in Alachua, Citrus, Duval, Hillsborough, Miami-Dade, Orange, Pasco and Pinellas and Seminole. Advisories are up in Bay, Brevard, Broward, Columbia, Holmes, Leon, Manatee, Martin, Palm Beach, Polk, Sarasota and Walton. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 19, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Dengue Dimer Epitope Antibodies Link to Protection From Severe Secondary Infection by November 14, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Dengue Dimer Epitope Antibodies Link to Protection From Severe Secondary Infection Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Antibodies targeting quaternary epitopes across the envelope protein dimer interface correlate with protection against severe dengue disease in patients undergoing secondary dengue virus infection, according to findings from clinical cohorts in Cambodia and Colombia. In contrast, antibodies directed against the conserved envelope fusion loop were found at significantly elevated proportions in hospitalized patients compared with individuals who experienced subclinical infections. Functionally, purified human antibody fractions directed against the soluble envelope dimer demonstrated potent virus neutralization and cross-neutralization against distinct serotypes while exhibiting limited enhancement of cellular infection. Conversely, antibodies recognizing the fusion loop mediated weak neutralization and pronounced antibody-dependent enhancement in Fc-receptor-bearing cells in vitro, clarifying how distinct antibody subsets directed toward the same viral surface protein can drive divergent clinical trajectories during natural post-primary dengue virus exposure. The dengue virus envelope glycoprotein is the primary target of human humoral immunity and is organized on mature virions into ninety homodimers arranged in an antiparallel head-to-tail lattice. Each monomeric envelope subunit comprises three structural regions designated domain one, domain two, and domain three, which together mediate cell attachment and acid-triggered membrane fusion. Within domain two, a hydrophobic fusion loop sequence remains highly conserved across all four dengue virus serotypes as well as related flaviviruses, yet its accessibility on mature virions is structurally constrained beneath neighboring envelope subunits. At the contact boundary formed between two paired envelope monomers, virus assembly generates a quaternary conformational target known as the envelope dimer epitope. While monoclonal antibodies against these respective sites have previously shown differing neutralization profiles in cell culture and animal models, their relative prevalence and direct association with human clinical severity across natural post-primary infections have historically remained unresolved. To investigate these epitope-specific antibody dynamics during active illness, investigators analyzed longitudinal plasma samples collected from children recruited into the prospective DENTHOM project across Kampong Thom and Siem Reap provinces in Cambodia. Patients admitted to Kampong Thom Provincial Hospital, Baray District Hospital, Stuong District Hospital, and Jayavarman VII Hospital with acute febrile illness were confirmed for secondary dengue virus serotype two infection using quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction alongside hemagglutination inhibition assays. Hospitalized cases were clinically classified according to World Health Organization criteria into classic dengue fever or severe manifestations comprising dengue hemorrhagic fever and dengue shock syndrome. Concurrently, household contact investigations surrounding laboratory-confirmed index cases identified infected individuals who developed subclinical infections, defined by absent or mild fever not exceeding thirty-eight degrees Celsius for at most two consecutive days and no more than one accompanying symptom such as rash, nausea, or aches. Using a multiplex microsphere-based immunoassay, the team tracked antibody binding against recombinant soluble envelope monomers, envelope domain three, and engineered soluble envelope dimers produced in Drosophila S2 cells harboring cysteine substitutions at residues leucine 107 and alanine 313. These engineered disulfide bonds preserve the envelope dimer conformation and prevent exposure of the internal fusion loop. By comparing untreated plasma binding against binding following competitive blockade with the pan-flavivirus monoclonal antibody clone 4G2, researchers quantified the exact proportions of fusion loop-targeting antibodies and dimer-specific quaternary antibodies throughout the acute, critical, early recovery, and late recovery phases. Across all post-primary infection phases, antibody concentrations recognizing domain three remained substantially lower than antibodies binding soluble envelope monomers and total soluble envelope dimers, demonstrating that domain three contributes only a modest share of the circulating polyclonal response in naturally infected pediatric patients. Epitope-specific antibody levels exhibited substantial inter-individual variability during early symptomatic presentation but increased markedly over time, reaching peak titers across the critical and early convalescent stages between four and fourteen days following symptom onset. During the acute phase spanning the initial three days of illness, detectable levels of dimer-specific antibodies were present in similar frequencies between subclinical and hospitalized individuals, and no differences in antibody proportions emerged when hospitalized patients were stratified by clinical severity. However, substantial divergence developed during the critical phase four to six days post-onset, which coincides with active viremia and the potential development of plasma leakage. Hospitalized patients showed significantly higher proportions of fusion loop-directed antibodies than individuals with subclinical infection, indicating that elevated proportions of poorly neutralizing, cross-reactive fusion loop antibodies in the critical window correlate with greater disease susceptibility. Among hospitalized children evaluated during the critical phase, the proportion of envelope dimer-specific antibodies proved significantly lower in severe dengue cases with hemorrhagic fever or shock syndrome than in children presenting with uncomplicated dengue fever. Median dimer-specific antibody proportions measured zero point twelve in severe cases compared with zero point thirty-seven in dengue fever, demonstrating a statistically significant protective association. To evaluate whether this immunological pattern extended across different viral serotypes and distinct host populations, the researchers examined an independent adult validation cohort from Cali and Bucaramanga, Colombia, comprising patients undergoing secondary dengue virus serotype one infection diagnosed by multiplex reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and high-avidity immunoglobulin G enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. In the Colombian cohort, hospitalized patients with classic dengue similarly exhibited higher median proportions of serotype one dimer-specific antibodies than those who progressed to severe disease, reinforcing the protective association across geographically distinct populations. To establish the mechanistic properties of these antibody populations directly from patient circulation rather than synthetic monoclonal surrogates, the investigators isolated total polyclonal immunoglobulin G from twelve Cambodian pediatric patients sampled during the critical phase. Utilizing sequential resin affinity chromatography coupled with site-specifically biotinylated recombinant envelope antigens, the authors successfully fractionated domain three antibodies, envelope dimer-specific antibodies, and fusion loop-reactive antibodies. Subsequent immunoassay binding validation confirmed that the dimer-specific fraction selectively recognized envelope dimers without cross-reacting with domain three, whereas the isolated fusion loop fraction bound preferentially to soluble monomeric envelope proteins displaying the exposed fusion motif while showing minimal reactivity against stabilized dimers or isolated domain three proteins. Functional evaluation using flow cytometry neutralization assays in Vero CCL-81 cells revealed that the purified envelope dimer-specific fraction possessed markedly superior neutralizing potency against dengue virus serotype two compared with fusion loop-binding antibodies. Dimer-specific antibodies achieved fifty percent viral neutralization at a median concentration of fifty-five point six nanograms per milliliter, whereas fusion loop antibodies required a significantly higher median concentration of one hundred forty-seven point four nanograms per milliliter to reach equivalent inhibition. Conversely, selective depletion of domain three, monomeric soluble envelope, and envelope dimer antibodies completely eliminated neutralization capacity while retaining residual infection enhancement, an effect likely maintained by non-neutralizing antibodies targeting structural pre-membrane proteins that remain on partially mature virus particles. Infection enhancement assays performed using engineered U937 monocyte cell lines expressing Fc-gamma receptors one, two-a, two-b, and three demonstrated that fusion loop antibodies generated substantially higher rates of antibody-dependent enhancement than dimer-specific or domain three fractions. At a test concentration of three hundred nanograms per milliliter, fusion loop-targeting antibodies induced productive infection in thirty point five percent of cells, compared with sixteen point three percent for domain three antibodies and fourteen point four percent for envelope dimer-specific antibodies. Even when normalized to their respective fifty percent inhibitory concentrations, fusion loop antibodies provoked over thirty percent cellular infection enhancement, roughly double the enhancement frequency observed for dimer-specific antibodies, confirming that fusion loop-directed antibodies display intrinsically heightened enhancing capacity under equivalent neutralization thresholds. Cross-neutralization experiments further underscored the distinct functional utility of envelope dimer antibodies when challenged with heterologous viral serotypes. When tested against dengue virus serotype one, dimer-specific antibodies isolated from serotype two-infected donors demonstrated potent cross-protective efficacy, achieving fifty percent inhibition at a median concentration of two point eighty-three nanograms per milliliter. In contrast, domain three fractions required a median of eighty-two point twenty-nine nanograms per milliliter, and fusion loop antibodies required four hundred eighty-one point one nanograms per milliliter to achieve fifty percent neutralization. These data confirm that while domain three-specific antibodies remain predominantly homotypic, human antibodies directed against the quaternary dimer interface mediate potent cross-serotype neutralization across genetically divergent dengue lineages. The study notes several methodological constraints and biological limitations that contextualize these immunological findings. Competitive blockade relied on mouse monoclonal antibody 4G2 to define fusion loop specificity, which might fail to detect human antibodies binding adjacent overlapping contacts or underestimate high-affinity human antibodies that outcompete the blocking clone. Furthermore, in vitro neutralization assays utilized virus stocks propagated in C6/36 mosquito cell lines, which harbor variable mixtures of immature and partially mature virions whose exposed structural surfaces can alter epitope accessibility compared with fully mature virus structures encountered in vivo. Clinically, determination of past dengue exposure relied on hemagglutination inhibition and antibody avidity assays, which cannot distinguish whether an individual has experienced exactly one prior infection or multiple tertiary and quaternary exposures that naturally skew antibody repertoires toward broader neutralizing profiles. Despite these considerations, the findings establish that the epitope specificity of the polyclonal envelope antibody repertoire represents a pivotal correlate of human dengue infection outcome. The data indicate that high relative proportions of fusion loop antibodies during the critical phase associate with symptomatic progression and hospitalization through Fc-mediated enhancement, whereas abundant quaternary dimer-targeting antibodies reduce disease severity and confer broad cross-neutralizing coverage. These observations offer direct immunological targets for vaccine design, indicating that next-generation immunization platforms should aim to present conformationally intact envelope dimers that elicit protective quaternary responses while minimizing the presentation of accessible, enhancement-prone fusion loop structures. Tay Nguyen Regional General Hospital (Dak Lak) is actively treating two children with severe Dengue hemorrhagic fever. Photo: Ha May Tay Nguyen Regional General Hospital has just reported to the Dak Lak Provincial Department of Health and the Provincial Center for Disease Control about two cases of children with severe Dengue hemorrhagic fever being treated at the Pediatric and Neonatal Intensive Care Units. The first case is patient H.S. N. (3 years old, residing in Krong Pac commune). The child started the disease on the evening of November 6 with symptoms of continuous high fever, dry cough, runny nose. On November 7, the family took the child to a medical facility for examination, then transferred him to the Central Highlands Regional General Hospital. Through testing, the patient had a positive NS1 result for Dengue hemorrhagic fever. By November 10, the child appeared with severe vomiting, liver damage, abdominal discharge and pleural damage. On November 11, the disease became severe with manifestations of shock, severe liver failure and blood clotting disorders. The patient was transferred to the Pediatric and Neonatal Intensive Care Units for treatment. After that, the child continued to develop grade IV respiratory failure, multiple organ failure, pleural effusion, gastrointestinal bleeding and severe thrombocytopenia. The hospital has held many consultations with Ho Chi Minh City Children's Hospital, implementing active resuscitation measures such as mechanical ventilation, continuous blood filtration, use of vasopressors and supportive treatment methods. According to a report on November 13, the patient is still in very serious condition, with a high risk of death. The second case is patient N.N.C. A. (9 years old, residing in Dak Sak commune, Lam Dong province). The child started the disease in the afternoon of November 8 with symptoms of fever, nosebleeds and vomiting. After many days of treatment at a medical facility, the disease progressed severely, platelets decreased deeply, and abdominal and pleural effusion appeared. On the evening of November 12, the child was transferred to the Central Highlands Regional General Hospital in a Dengue hemorrhagic fever condition with signs of shock, respiratory failure and severe thrombocytopenia. At the hospital, the child was treated with resuscitation, respiratory support with non-invasive machinery, intravenous fluids and albumin. By November 13, the child still showed signs of respiratory failure, abdominal distension, gastrointestinal bleeding and nosebleeds. The above two cases show that Dengue hemorrhagic fever in children can progress severely, causing shock, respiratory failure and damage to many organs. Parents need to closely monitor the health developments of children, take children to medical facilities when there are abnormal signs, and not be subjective when the child has reduced fever. Get Finance Plus Florida's 524-case dengue outbreak centered in Tampa Bay raises urgent travel insurance questions for Canadian snowbirds Melanie Huddart Sat, November 14, 2026 at 8:00 a.m. EST 7 min read Close up of mosquito biting someone, elderly couple walking on the beach Florida is currently experiencing its largest dengue fever outbreak in decades — just in time for Canadian snowbirds to start planning their winter away in the Sunshine State. The Florida Department of Health, the state's public health agency, has confirmed 524 locally acquired cases of the virus so far this year, according to its weekly report for Oct. 25 to 31. That's up from 485 a week earlier. Locally acquired means the virus was spread by mosquitoes in Florida, rather than picked up while travelling abroad. Most cases were reported in Hillsborough County, around Tampa. Most dengue cases are reported as typically mild, but can require a trip to the hospital if symptoms worsen. But if you're a Canadian in Florida, your provincial health care plan will provide minimal coverage. Whether you are the hook to pay for the rest will depend on what your coverage includes. Don't Miss A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change Warren Buffett used these 4 solid, repeatable money rules to turn $9,800 into a $150B fortune. Here's how to apply them to your own life I'm 65, tired of working and have very little savings — is it possible to live off CPP alone? Yes, but you'll need to make these 3 big sacrifices How serious is Florida's dengue outbreak? Florida's outbreak is the largest in the continental U.S. in several decades, according to the Associated Press, the U.S.-based news agency. Data from state health departments and medical journals suggest it marks the most locally acquired cases in a calendar year for any U.S. state since at least the 1940s. Florida's previous worst year was 2023, when just under 200 cases were reported. This year's count is already more than double that. The outbreak is centralized in one of the most popular destinations for Canadian snowbirds: the Tampa Bay area. As of Oct. 31, Hillsborough County had recorded 407 local cases and Pinellas County 80. Ten other counties have also reported cases, including Orange (Orlando), Miami-Dade and Palm Beach. In September, Florida confirmed its first dengue death of the year: an 80-year-old Tampa woman who passed away on Sept. 4. Dengue is contracted through bites from mosquitoes carrying the virus, not from person-to-person contact. Symptoms include fever, a severe headache and intense joint and muscle pain, which is why dengue is nicknamed "breakbone fever." Most people have mild symptoms or none at all and recover within one to two weeks, but severe cases can be life-threatening and require hospital care. Story Continues On Oct. 15, Global Affairs Canada (GAC), the federal department responsible for travel advice, added an outbreak monitoring alert for dengue in Florida to its U.S. travel advice page. The overall risk level for the U.S. didn't change. It remains at "take normal security precautions," the lowest of GAC's four levels. Will your provincial coverage kick in if you get sick in Florida? At best, you might get the very minimal costs covered. Under the Canada Health Act, provinces must pay for emergency care received outside Canada based on what they would have paid for similar services at home. In practice, most provinces pay a flat daily amount that falls short of that standard. The Canadian Snowbird Association (CSA), a non-profit that advocates for Canadian travellers, has lobbied provinces to reimburse at in-province rates. The Ontario Health Insurance Plan (OHIP) Out of Country Travellers Program pays up to CA$400 a day for emergency care in an intensive care unit (ICU), coronary care unit or operating room, and up to CA$200 per day for lower levels of inpatient care. For emergency outpatient services, such as an emergency room (ER) visit, it pays up to CA$50 a day or the amount billed, whichever is less. Doctors' services are reimbursed at Ontario fee-schedule rates. Several provinces pay even less, though. Alberta, Saskatchewan and Quebec cap emergency inpatient care at CA$100 a day, while British Columbia pays CA$75 a day. These fixed amounts cover only a sliver of U.S. hospital bills. B.C.'s Ministry of Health warns that a day in a U.S. hospital often costs more than US$1,000 and can reach US$10,000 in intensive care. In Florida, hospitals spent an average of US$2,487 to US$3,382 per adjusted inpatient day in 2024, depending on the type of hospital, according to KFF, a U.S. non-profit health policy research organization. That's what it costs hospitals to provide care, not what they bill patients. Physician fees, tests and ambulance rides come on top, so even a short hospital stay can add up quickly. Read More: How financially stable am I? You're doing better than most if you check off just 1 of these 3 boxes Will your travel insurance cover dengue? In most cases, a sudden illness like dengue falls under the emergency medical portion of your travel insurance policy. But some details in the fine print can determine whether your claim is covered. Travel advisories Typically, Canadian insurance policies will state limits or exclusions based on Ottawa's warnings against non-essential travel, or all travel to specific destinations. While the U.S. is well below an advisory of this level, and the dengue flag shouldn't be enough to trigger a blanket exclusion, be vigilant in understanding how your policy treats a specific health warning — the wording matters most. Pre-existing health conditions Snowbirds usually represent an older demographic, and are more likely to have health conditions. If dengue further complicates an existing condition, your insurer will examine your medical history against your medical questionnaire. If you withheld a medical condition on your questionnaire, or if your condition or medication changed during your policy's stability period — the window before departure when a pre-existing condition must stay unchanged to be covered — you could be denied coverage for claims related to that condition. Trip duration Many snowbird insurance policies cap the number of days you can spend outside of Canada. If your stay runs past that limit, you could be uninsured over those extra days. The Travel Health Insurance Association of Canada (THIA), which represents the country's travel insurance industry, has long urged travellers to make sure they're fully covered. "With U.S. medical costs among the highest in the world, proper coverage is non-negotiable," THIA executive director Will McAleer said when the association released its 2025 winter travel survey. What can you do to protect yourself? Florida's dengue outbreak doesn't mean cancelling your winter travel plans altogether. But it's a good reminder to carefully review your coverage, while limiting your exposure to mosquitoes. Buy insurance coverage before you take off. Only relying on your provincial plan is risky. Get travel medical insurance to cover your entire time away Answer the medical questionnaire carefully and honestly. List every condition, name every medication and make your insurer aware of any changes before you leave — even minor ones Ask about travel advisories. Ask your broker or insurer how your policy applies if Canada's cross-border travel advice changes while you're away Check your employer or retiree group benefits. Some plans include out-of-country coverage, but it may be more restrictive than a snowbird policy Know who to call in an emergency. Save your insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance number in your phone. Many policies require you to call before receiving treatment, or within 24 to 48 hours of an emergency, and to follow the advice to keep your coverage Prevent mosquito bites. Use insect repellent, wear long sleeves and pants, empty standing water around your property and limit your time outdoors — dengue-carrying mosquitoes can bite at any time of day, not just at dusk. Watch for symptoms. If you're suddenly hit with a fever, severe headache or body aches, see a doctor immediately. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 19, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Galectin-3 Restricts Dengue Virus Infection Through Envelope Binding and Immune Signaling by November 15, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Galectin-3 Restricts Dengue Virus Infection Through Envelope Binding and Immune Signaling Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram The host protein galectin-3 restricts dengue virus serotype 2 infection by directly binding to the viral envelope glycoprotein, inhibiting viral entry, and enhancing pro-inflammatory NF-κB signaling pathways, according to laboratory and animal findings reported in Virology Journal. Currently, no antiviral therapy is approved for dengue virus, an important pathogen whose pathogenesis remains a major challenge. Galectin-3 is a recognized β-galactoside-binding lectin known to modulate several distinct viral infections, yet its precise mechanistic role in dengue virus infection and disease development had not been previously established. To systematically determine how this lectin influences viral replication, the research team employed a green fluorescent protein-tagged DENV-2 reporter virus across multiple cellular experimental conditions. The investigators evaluated the biological consequences of administering purified recombinant galectin-3, depleting cellular protein levels through targeted knockdown, and increasing cellular protein abundance through experimental overexpression. In addition to assessing replication kinetics, the authors analyzed specific steps in the viral life cycle, focusing on initial viral attachment to host cells and subsequent viral internalization. Initial cellular observations revealed that active DENV-2 infection led to a marked down-regulation of endogenous galectin-3 expression within host cells. When the researchers introduced recombinant galectin-3 into the extracellular environment, the protein caused a dose-dependent reduction in both DENV-2 infectivity and the production of infectious progeny virus. A comparable inhibitory outcome was observed when cells were treated with conditioned medium containing naturally secreted galectin-3, demonstrating that extracellular forms of the lectin exert antiviral activity against the virus. The inhibitory effect of galectin-3 proved to be highly specific and dependent on defined carbohydrate recognition mechanisms. The antiviral restriction exerted by the protein was effectively reversed by the addition of lactose, a known competitive carbohydrate ligand, as well as by the galectin-3-neutralizing monoclonal antibody B2C10. Conversely, neither the control carbohydrate sucrose nor non-specific control immunoglobulin G reversed the observed viral inhibition, confirming that the protective effect relies on specific glycan binding mediated by the lectin. Biochemical and molecular evaluations demonstrated that galectin-3 physically binds the dengue virus envelope glycoprotein, directly hindering both viral attachment and viral internalization into target cells. To clarify the structural basis of this interaction, computational in silico molecular docking was performed against the viral envelope protein. The docking simulations showed that galectin-3 is compatible with engaging both known envelope glycosylation sites, with aggregate computational binding scores favoring interaction at the asparagine-67 (Asn67) glycosylation site. Genetic manipulation of endogenous galectin-3 levels further corroborated its protective role during intracellular infection. Experimental knockdown of endogenous galectin-3 significantly enhanced DENV-2 replication, whereas the overexpression of galectin-3 successfully suppressed viral replication. Concurrently, galectin-3 amplified intracellular NF-κB activation and increased the downstream expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines, specifically interleukin-6, interleukin-8, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, and interleukin-1-beta, notably doing so without altering transcripts for type I interferons. To determine whether these in vitro antiviral mechanisms translate into protection within a living organism, the researchers assessed disease outcomes in neonatal galectin-3 knockout mice inoculated intracerebrally with DENV-2. Mice lacking galectin-3 exhibited significantly earlier mortality, carried elevated viral loads within brain tissues, and suffered more severe neuropathology compared to wild-type control animals. These animal results confirmed that endogenous galectin-3 deficiency substantially worsens disease progression and neuropathology in vivo. Together, these findings indicate that galectin-3 restricts dengue virus serotype 2 by binding envelope glycans to block entry and by promoting NF-κB-dependent pro-inflammatory responses. Because galectin-3 deficiency exacerbates infection severity in animal models, the study highlights the lectin as a potential host-directed therapeutic target against dengue virus. However, because these evaluations were conducted in cell culture systems and intracerebrally inoculated neonatal mice, further investigation is required before inferring clinical efficacy or therapeutic utility in human dengue patients. supplementary_news.content_title: Thai dengue toll at 47 as southern Region 11 reports 1.7 times national level
supplementary_news.content: Thailand has recorded 47 deaths and 34,875 dengue cases nationwide as of November 7. - Southern Health Region 11 is a key area of concern, reporting a dengue rate approximately 1.7 times the national level. - Authorities are concerned that flooding and standing water in the south are creating more breeding grounds for mosquitoes, increasing infection risk. - Despite the southern outbreak, the cumulative number of dengue cases nationwide in 2026 is lower than in the previous year. The Thai government has instructed health workers and village health volunteers to strengthen dengue awareness in flood-affected southern Thailand, amid concerns that standing water could create more mosquito breeding grounds and increase the risk of infection. Deputy government spokeswoman Ploytalay Laksameesangchan said on Sunday (November 15, 2026) that southern health regions were reporting the highest numbers of dengue cases, although the cumulative national total remained below the previous year’s level. Citing the Department of Disease Control’s Division of Epidemiology, she reported 34,875 dengue cases and 47 deaths nationwide through November 7. Most patients were of school or working age, while deaths were concentrated among older adults. Health Regions 11 and 12 in southern Thailand currently reported the highest case numbers, according to Ploytalay. For Health Region 11, she cited a figure approximately 1.7 times the national level, with persistent rainfall identified as a possible contributing factor. The statement did not specify the statistical measure used for that comparison. The government expressed concern that flooding and standing water could provide additional breeding grounds for Aedes mosquitoes, increasing the risk of dengue transmission in affected communities. Public health personnel and village health volunteers have been instructed to alert residents, improve awareness and help communities prepare, with the aim of preventing further infections. Despite concerns in the South, the cumulative number of dengue cases nationwide in 2026 was lower than in 2025, Ploytalay noted. She identified August as the peak period for reported infections, citing approximately 1,450 cases compared with about 2,700 in 2025. The statement did not specify the reporting interval covered by those figures. We use cookies and similar technologies to enhance your user experience. supplementary_news.content_title: 伊朗德黑兰登革热出现风险:Aedes生态学、气候、城市环境决定因素与公共卫生准备的综合评价 - 生物通
supplementary_news.content: 伊朗德黑兰登革热出现风险:Aedes生态学、气候、城市环境决定因素与公共卫生准备的综合评价 《Public Health in Practice》:Dengue emergence risk in Tehran, Iran: An integrative review of Aedes ecology, climate, urban environmental determinants, and public health preparedness 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月18日 来源:Public Health in Practice 2.2 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 目标:综合有关Aedes蚊生态学及潜在定殖、气候与环境适宜性、流行病学与城市决定因素,以及伊朗德黑兰登革热出现相关公共卫生监测与准备的现有证据。该综述还旨在区分环境接受性(environmental receptivity,指可能支持媒介若引入后生存繁殖的气候、生态、城市或社会条件)与潜在媒介定殖(vector establishment,指媒介种群持续繁殖)和已记录的本地登革热传播(autochthonous transmission,指无明确输入病例的本地传播),并识别关键证据缺口与监测优先事项。研究设计:结构化叙述性/整合性综述。方法:进行结构化文献检索,覆盖2000年1月至2025年3月的出版物及相关公开信息。检索PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science、ScienceDirect、Google Scholar及选定的伊朗机构来源。证据按四个预设域综合:Aedes媒介生态学与潜在定殖;气候与环境适宜性;流行病学、人群层面、城市与基础设施决定因素;媒介监测、控制与公共卫生准备。选择12项核心研究进行聚焦的定性与整合分析综合。证据按其地理相关性和方法学基础解释,区分德黑兰直接发现与伊朗、区域、国际及基于模型的证据。结果:现有证据未证明德黑兰存在Aedes aegypti或Aedes albopictus种群的持续定殖或持续本地登革热传播。然而,气候变率、变暖趋势、城市环境条件、潜在繁殖栖息地、人口流动及区域昆虫学证据提示未来环境接受性可能相关。气候与空间模型提示在变暖情景下Aedes媒介和登革热相关传播的环境适宜性可能扩大,但这些预测并未确立当地媒介种群或证明德黑兰登革热传播。标准化纵向昆虫学监测以及整合的流行病学和实验室监测仍存在重要局限。结论:德黑兰最好被描述为具有潜在且演变中的登革热接受性,而非已建立登革热传播。现有证据不足以断定该市已建立持续Aedes种群或持续本地登革热传播。有必要开展标准化纵向昆虫学监测、整合的流行病学与实验室监测、环境评估和协调的公共卫生准备,以降低不确定性并促进潜在登革热出现的早期发现。 研究背景:登革热(dengue fever)是全球重要蚊媒病毒病,其流行病学分布与Aedes媒介生态、地理范围、季节活动和种群动态密切相关。主要媒介Aedes aegypti(埃及伊蚊)和Aedes albopictus(白纹伊蚊)适应人类主导环境,可利用人工容器、家庭储水设施、废弃物及其他小型水体。媒介生态适宜性受温度、降水、湿度、繁殖栖息地、植被与土地利用、住房特征、人类行为和人口流动等多因素影响。城市登革热出现是多阶段过程,需要适宜生态环境、具传播能力媒介的存在或定殖、登革病毒引入、足够的人—媒介接触以及上述要素的时空重叠,不能由单一环境或流行病学指标推断。伊朗目前并非登革热地方性流行传播已建立的国家,伊朗若干地区已有Aedes生态和虫媒病毒监测证据,但德黑兰尚未证明持续Aedes aegypti或Aedes albopictus种群定殖或持续本地登革热传播;同时,缺乏充分纵向昆虫学监测不应被解释为瞬时引入或局限媒介种群绝不可能发生。德黑兰人口密集、城市形态与住房/储水/垃圾/排水等空间异质性明显,可能构成环境接受性;气候变暖、降水变率和模型提示的适宜区变化可提供机制背景,但气候适宜性不等于媒介定殖,模型预测也不等于德黑兰传播预测。输入性登革热感染是病毒引入机会,但不等于后续本地传播。常规蚊控可能不足以区分瞬时引入与持续种群。因此,研究人员开展结构化叙述性/整合性综述,综合异质证据,不估计未来传播的定量概率,而在于区分环境接受性、潜在媒介定殖与已证实传播,识别证据缺口和监测优先事项。研究结论提示德黑兰应被视为具有潜在且演变中的登革热接受性,而非已建立登革热传播;其意义在于支持标准化纵向昆虫学监测、整合流行病学与实验室监测、环境评估和协调公共卫生准备,以降低不确定性并促进早期发现。 欢迎领域“高通量小分子筛选解决方案”>> 领 取 方法概述:研究人员采用结构化叙述性/整合性综述,检索2000年1月至2025年3月PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science、ScienceDirect、Google Scholar及选定伊朗机构来源;以Aedes生态与潜在定殖、气候环境适宜性、流行病学/城市基础设施决定因素、媒介监测控制与公共卫生准备四域框架筛选;两名评价者独立评估,最终纳入12项核心研究进行定性整合;按地理相关性区分德黑兰、伊朗其他地区、可比国际环境和区域/全球模型证据;描述性使用IRIMO公开气象资料,并用Excel/QGIS制作概念可视化;未进行Meta分析、合并效应估计或原始生态位/气候—传播模型。无原始样本队列。 研究结果:Aedes媒介生态学与潜在定殖:基于伊朗昆虫学与虫媒病毒监测研究及国际生态研究,现有证据未提供德黑兰足够标准化、纵向且物种确认的数据以证明Aedes aegypti或Aedes albopictus持续定殖;其他伊朗地区证据可提供媒介区系和生态背景,但不能替代德黑兰本地证据。气候与环境适宜性:基于国际生态/气候模型、区域与全球空间模型、IRIMO描述性气象资料及德黑兰气候证据,温度、降水、暖期持续时间和城市气候条件可能影响Aedes适宜性;模型提示变暖情景下环境适宜区可能扩大,但未确立当地媒介种群或登革热传播,也未建立德黑兰特异性动力降尺度气候—登革热传播模型。流行病学、人群、城市与基础设施决定因素:基于伊朗/国际流行病学与城市环境文献,未证明德黑兰持续本地登革热传播;伊朗登革热活动更符合旅行相关或地理输入风险;人口流动和输入病例是病毒引入机会,但不等于本地传播;人口密度、住房、家庭/社区储水、垃圾管理、卫生、排水和社区行为可能影响繁殖栖息地与人—媒介接触,但其独立贡献未量化。媒介监测、控制与公共卫生准备:基于伊朗和国际虫媒病毒准备文献,需要整合纵向昆虫学监测、输入登革热流行病学监测、实验室确认、媒介鉴定和协调响应;常规蚊控可能不足以早期识别新引入或地理局限的Aedes种群;现有证据不足以量化德黑兰总体准备水平、建立验证的准备评分或经验性全市监测强度、诱捕密度和干预阈值。跨域综合:证据呈现分级模式,当前无持续本地传播及持续媒介定殖的直接证据较强,而未来环境接受性证据较广但多为间接;德黑兰应被描述为具有潜在且演变中的登革热接受性,而非已建立传播的城市。 讨论部分总结:该综述强调登革热出现风险是多维、演变中的过程,不能归因于单一气候、昆虫学或流行病学决定因素。环境接受性、媒介定殖和持续本地传播是不同推断层级,不能互换;气候适宜性、城市微生境或潜在繁殖环境不应解释为已建立Aedes种群,输入感染也不应解释为本地传播。气候模型证据提供潜在环境接受性变化的机制背景,但尺度较宽,不能作为德黑兰传播预测;城市环境特征可能是局部接受性的调节因素,但其幅度和空间分布未充分量化;人口流动是潜在病毒引入桥梁,但单独不足以支持持续传播。监测与准备应整合纵向昆虫学、流行病学、实验室和环境信息,但未建立经验验证的诱捕密度、监测频率、地区干预阈值或准备评分。优势包括多维耦合、按地理与推断接近度分层、12项核心研究透明整合、不将无证据等同于不能引入,并连接环境接受性与定殖/病毒引入/持续传播;局限包括德黑兰特异性纵向昆虫学证据有限且异质、借用其他地区与模型证据、定性综合、无原始生态位/预测GIS/气候—传播模型、概念图非验证指数、非系统综述且未前瞻注册。研究结论翻译:该综述发现支持对德黑兰登革热出现风险采取谨慎、面向准备的解释。当前证据未证明该市存在持续本地登革热传播或Aedes aegypti或Aedes albopictus持续定殖。同时,气候与城市环境条件、人口流动、区域昆虫学证据及国际生态和气候研究提示一组可能影响未来环境接受性的情况。这些发现不应被解释为登革热传播即将发生或不可避免,而表明从环境接受性到媒介定殖、再到本地传播的转变仍是未解决的实证问题。最适当的公共卫生应对不是假定地方性传播,而是通过标准化纵向昆虫学监测、媒介与流行病学监测整合、相关城市环境决定因素表征以及媒介和病原鉴定实验室能力来降低不确定性;此类本地证据将为判断环境接受性变化是否转化为持续媒介种群或本地传播提供更强依据,并减少对地理遥远生态观察和广尺度气候模型的依赖。作者:Ebrahim Abbasi|Asghar Talbalaghi 研究背景:登革热(dengue fever)是全球重要蚊媒病毒病,其流行病学分布与Aedes媒介生态、地理范围、季节活动和种群动态密切相关。主要媒介Aedes aegypti(埃及伊蚊)和Aedes albopictus(白纹伊蚊)适应人类主导环境,可利用人工容器、家庭储水设施、废弃物及其他小型水体。媒介生态适宜性受温度、降水、湿度、繁殖栖息地、植被与土地利用、住房特征、人类行为和人口流动等多因素影响。城市登革热出现是多阶段过程,需要适宜生态环境、具传播能力媒介的存在或定殖、登革病毒引入、足够的人—媒介接触以及上述要素的时空重叠,不能由单一环境或流行病学指标推断。伊朗目前并非登革热地方性流行传播已建立的国家,伊朗若干地区已有Aedes生态和虫媒病毒监测证据,但德黑兰尚未证明持续Aedes 上一期,已有证据或理论提示蚊媒病毒具备输血传播能力。当前基孔肯雅病毒、登革病毒、寨卡病毒全球发病率高、传播媒介分布广泛,已经成为输血安全面临的新挑战。世界卫生组织(WHO)呼吁各输血中心掌握各类新发输血传播感染的流行病学信息,评估其对献血者筛选标准以及血液制品供应可能造成的影响。 截至发文,基孔肯雅病毒尚未报告经输血传播的病例,但美国血库协会等机构发出警示,人群无症状感染比例高达 3%~28%,且感染者病毒血症水平高,具备理论传播风险,同时法国曾报道 1 起针刺意外造成的医源性基孔肯雅病毒传播事件。登革病毒病是全球发病率、死亡率最高的虫媒病毒病。自2002年起,中国香港、新加坡、巴西、巴基斯坦、波多黎各均报告多起登革病毒输血传播案例。寨卡病毒感染者中约80%感染者无临床症状,巴西已有血小板输注传播寨卡病毒的病例报道。 这类病毒的出现对血液制备供应带来切实威胁,直接影响献血者筛选标准与血液库存。遵照 WHO 建议,本研究旨在结合筛查手段(病毒血症阳性率、血清阳性率、抗原检测)以及地理区域,汇总发表文献中献血者基孔肯雅、登革、寨卡病毒流行率。 二、研究方法 【研究问题PICOS 框架】 项目 研究内容 Population研究对象 各类献血者,包含全血捐献者、单采成分献血者,来自任意地理区域,接受目标病毒任意检测手段筛查。 Intervention干预措施 采用不同技术检测抗体、抗原或者核酸。 Comparison对照 不设置对照。 Outcome结局 不同检测手段、不同地理区域报道的各病毒流行率。 Study研究类型 所有原始研究 【检索策略】 (1)数据库:MEDLINE、Embase、Scopus。 (2)检索时间:从数据库建库至 2020-03-28,每周更新文献,持续至2020-08-07。 (3)检索方法: ▪三库采用自由词检索,检索式:“transfusion” AND “Dengue”;“transfusion” AND “Chikungunya”;“transfusion” AND “Zika”;“blood donation” AND “Dengue”;“blood donation” AND “Chikungunya”;“blood donation” AND “Zika”。 ▪MEDLINE 同时使用医学主题词(MeSH)检索:“blood transfusion” AND “Zika virus”;“blood donors” AND “Zika virus”;“blood transfusion” AND “Dengue”;“blood donors” AND “Dengue”;“blood transfusion” AND “Chikungunya virus”;“blood donors” AND “Chikungunya virus”。 ▪Embase 数据库使用 Emtree 叙词表检索:“blood transfusion” AND “Zika virus”;“blood donor” AND “Zika virus”;“blood transfusion” AND “Chikungunya”;“blood donor” AND “Chikungunya”;“blood transfusion” AND “Dengue”;“blood donor” AND “Dengue”。 (4)文献管理:文献题录导入 Mendeley软件 。 【文献筛选】 (1)纳入标准: ▪语种不限 ▪报道献血者(普通全血献血者、各类单采献血者)病毒流行率 ▪文献类型:包含原始论著、短篇报告、读者来信、会议摘要 ▪报告阳性样本数与总样本数 ▪写明筛查检测类型(血清学、抗原、核酸扩增 NAT)以及研究人群的地理信息。 (2)排除标准: ▪研究对象非献血人群,例如普通患者、儿童、孕妇、普通非献血人群以及其他不明人群。 (3)筛选方法: ▪由一名综述作者完成文献筛选,未做评价者间一致性检验。开展评价者内部一致性复核。同一篇全文经过两轮评估,两次均满足纳入排除标准才纳入本综述。 ▪同一篇文献包含两组差异显著的研究人群(如同时包含非洲和欧洲人群,流行率差异明显),则在分析中拆分。同一人群使用多种检测方法,不同检测结果分开分析。多篇文献研究人群重叠时,选择样本量最大的文献纳入。 【统计分析】 (1)数据提取: ▪一名作者提取流行率与人群数据,录入综合荟萃分析软件 CMA,第二名作者复核录入准确性。 ▪合并阳性例数和筛查总人数,计算三种病毒基于不同筛查手段的献血人群总体阳性率。 ▪当某一地理区域至少有3项纳入研究时,按地理/国家分层分析。在条件允许时,区分地方流行区/疫情暴发区、非流行区,计算流行率比值。 (2)质量评价: ▪采用 STROBE 清单评价横断面研究与会议摘要方法学质量。 ▪读者来信不做评价。 (3)统计分析: ▪结果以流行率及 95% 置信区间表示,绘制森林图。 ▪采用 I2 评价各检测方法下研究间异质性。 ▪分析使用 CMA 2 版本(Borenstein, Hedges, Higgins, & Rothstein, 2005)。 三、关键结果 【样本情况】 本研究纳入 18 篇关于基孔肯雅病毒、71 篇关于登革病毒、27 篇关于寨卡病毒的文献。 【基孔肯雅病毒流行率】 基孔肯雅病毒IgG抗体总体血清阳性率为21.6%(95%CI:20.6%~22.5%),部分研究血清阳性率为 0,卢旺达 2015 年研究血清阳性率高达 63.0%(95% CI:59.8%~66.2%)。非洲地区血清阳性率最高为37.8%(95% CI:36.2%~39.4%)。流行率比值为 24.4。仅检索到 1 篇献血者基孔肯雅 IgM 血清阳性率报道,为 5.5%(95% CI:3.1%~9.7%)。核酸检测(NAT)总体流行率 0.5%(95% CI:0.4%~0.5%);波多黎各 2014 年筛查最高,1.9%(95% CI:1.4%~2.4%)。地方流行或疫情暴发地区 NAT 阳性率 0.6%(95% CI:0.6%~0.7%),非流行地区为 0。 表1 献血人群基孔肯雅病毒全球流行率(按研究人群) 地区 (Region) 事件数 疫情暴发地区核酸检测(NAT)检出病毒血症献血者比例较高:基孔肯雅病毒最高 1.9%,登革病毒最高 5.5%,寨卡病毒最高 2.8%。这类献血者没有临床症状,但体内病毒载量高,存在切实的输血传播风险。 【结论二】疫情暴发或流行地区需要重点关注 疫情暴发地区核酸检测(NAT)检出病毒血症献血者比例较高,非疫情暴发地区的核酸检测阳性率几乎为零。登革病毒 IgG 高血清阳性率见于高度地方流行区或者大规模疫情之后。基孔肯雅与登革病毒 IgG 血清阳性率整体较高,高阳性率地区反复暴发疫情,如撒哈拉以南非洲。流行区/非流行区流行率比值:CHIKV 24.4、DENV(IgG)13.9、ZIKV 9.0。提示疫情暴发或流行地区蚊媒病毒输血传播风险相对高。 【结论三】病毒流行率高提示存在更多无症状献血者 血清阳性率可以反映人群既往暴露水平。既往暴露水平高,提示存在更多无症状感染献血者。血清阳性率本身具备重要流行病学价值,是评估风险规模的重要参考。基于IgG抗体检测得到的总体血清阳性率:基孔肯雅病毒 21.6%,登革病毒 24.0%,寨卡病毒 5.1%。三种虫媒病毒较高的血清阳性率提示病毒在人群中广泛循环,与无症状感染献血者风险升高相关。但非洲献血人群寨卡血清阳性率很低,提示寨卡病毒在非洲传播有限,这点和登革、基孔肯雅病毒不同。 【结论四】血清阳性率高的地区共性 血清阳性率高的地区存在共性,包括热带气候,有明显雨季,植被和水资源丰富,经济水平较低。提示需要多措并举降低虫媒病毒输血传播风险,既包括气候、水资源、农业森林资源宏观环境政策,也包括媒介防控社区措施、湿地水资源保护、完善卫生系统。 【结论五】输血安全防控策略启示 ▪完善献血者问诊,询问相关感染症状;告知献血者献血后数周出现相关症状要及时上报。但上述手段无法识别无症状病毒血症献血者。 ▪对红细胞成分实施隔离存放,推迟放行,等待病毒潜伏期结束。该措施需要献血筛选、血液警戒工作人员充分培训,同时需要献血者自我健康监测配合。 ▪疫情暴发时暂停当地采血(如意大利2007基孔肯雅疫情)。但资源匮乏地区很难落地实施。 ▪开展献血者筛查,优先核酸检测;核酸不可及的地区,可采用床旁快速检测(免疫检测、RT-PCR、RT-LAMP)。针对三种病毒,这类快速检测灵敏度和特异度尚可接受。 ▪条件允许时,使用病原体灭活技术。该类手段已经证实对多种虫媒病毒有效。 编者评论 从个案到群体调查结果来看,蚊媒病毒输血传播风险确实存在且不容忽视。但是不同地区的无症状病毒血症者存量存在差异,风险程度不一,需根据实际情况评估。此外,同一地区不同阶段也存在不同的风险。疫情暴发期间,因公众广泛暴露,无症状病毒血症献血者相对增多,输血传播风险也相应有所升高,需要重点关注。相对而言,非流行地区或非疫情暴发地区献血者处于低流行率,是否有必要采取常态化防控措施,仍需更多证据。 当前群体调查结果显示,不同研究所使用诊断方法差异大,灵敏度特异度各不相同,自建检验性能参差不齐。同时,病毒核酸检测由于成本高、操作复杂、检测配套要求高等因素,很多地区无法常规开展,非洲地区无一研究使用核酸筛查。因此,在选择筛查策略和筛查工具时,需要综合研判。从卫生经济学理论角度看,核酸筛查更适合用于目标人群筛查策略,与之相对,血清学检测则更可能用于大规模人群筛查。实践中如何选择,仍需要更多卫生经济学实践证据的支持。 需要提醒的是,使用血清学检测时,应充分评估蚊媒病毒之间的血清学交叉反应。非洲基孔肯雅 IgG 阳性结果中部分阳性样本中和试验显示奥尼永–奥尼永病毒、马亚罗病毒滴度更高,存在甲病毒交叉干扰。登革病毒与其他黄病毒同样存在交叉反应,但登革相关研究大多开展中和试验。本综述纳入的寨卡全部研究均使用中和试验。 下一期,我们将分享输血传播登革热防控策略的评估与选择。敬请期待。 上一篇:输血传播蚊媒传染病系列|输血传播登革热是否构成潜在的公共卫生威胁?
